item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
A US-brokered ceasefire now covers Oleshky and has been extended across the Kherson region, while local ceasefires operate in other frontline cities. Putin is courting African leaders at a Moscow summit and held a rare phone call with the leaders of Norway and Finland, seeking to expand Russia's footprint in Africa. Trump is exploring lifting sanctions on a Russian flagship investment fund, and Zelenskyy urged faster delivery of Patriot missiles while pushing back against Musk, praised by Putin as a "genius" for his Starshield system. The conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

The IDF has killed several Hamas operatives and commanders in recent Gaza strikes, including six operatives and three commanders. Israel's parliamentary election remains deadlocked, with Netanyahu's bloc leading but short of a majority and record Arab turnout creating a dilemma for the opposition. item.title: Iran and the regional confrontation: the situation
item.description:
Iran is pressing Qatar and the region to reopen the Strait of Hormuz while Houthi missiles and drones continue striking Saudi oil facilities and airports, prompting the reopening of Riyadh Airport after weeks of disruption. The United States has lost roughly 25% of its Reaper drones as the war depletes its arsenal and is weighing renewed strikes on Iran, driving oil prices above $117 a barrel. Qatar has urged Iran to show goodwill by ending threats and is reportedly ready to trade UN inspector access for sanctions relief, while Gulf states are working on a multipart peace deal to avert a renewal of the US-Iran war. War costs are estimated at $47 billion, according to the U.S. military.

item.description:
The Houthis have launched ballistic missiles at Yemen's Aden airport twice in one day, prompting evacuation warnings, and have also fired missiles toward Saudi Arabia, with debris striking a building in Riyadh and an intercept over Taif, while a missile claim targeted the Ras Tanura refinery. Egypt's parliament has approved military support to defend Saudi Arabia, linking the conflict to broader regional involvement. Gulf states are negotiating a multipart peace deal to avoid a renewed US-Iran war. Russian satellites are being used to guide Houthi strikes on Saudi targets, contributing to higher oil prices. item.description:

Syrian forces killed a French jihadist in a shootout in Harem and another French extremist in Idlib, and two Syrian defence ministry personnel were killed by unidentified gunmen in Idlib. Jordan and Syria have reopened a border crossing and agreed to a joint investigation, while Jordanian officials cite a security vacuum in the south. item.description:

Somalia denied that Turkish F‑16 aircraft struck its own positions during the clashes, and US forces were accused of weaponising floods by trapping women and children.
